name: Atenolol
summary: A hydrophilic, cardioselective beta-1 blocker used once daily for hypertension, angina, and post-MI care. Unlike carvedilol, bisoprolol, or metoprolol succinate, it has not shown mortality benefit in heart failure and is not used for HFrEF.
mechanism: Selectively blocks beta-1 adrenergic receptors, reducing heart rate, myocardial contractility, and renin release.

dosing.renalAdjustment: Reduce dose in renal impairment (e.g. 50 mg every other day when CrCl <35 mL/min)

safety.lactation: Present in breast milk; use with caution
warnings: Do not stop abruptly — rebound tachycardia/ischemia risk
Caution in asthma/COPD despite relative beta-1 selectivity
Bradycardia and hypotension, especially with other antihypertensives
safety.overdose: Bradycardia, hypotension, bronchospasm; treat with atropine, glucagon, and supportive care.

clinicalPearls: Hydrophilicity means little CNS penetration — less vivid dreams/insomnia than lipophilic beta blockers.
Not recommended for HFrEF: lacks the mortality benefit shown for carvedilol, bisoprolol, and metoprolol succinate.
good: Once-daily hypertension/angina therapy with low CNS side-effect burden.
bad: Asthma, decompensated heart failure, or renal impairment without dose reduction.
